title: Split Array Largest Sum
question: Why can binary search be used on the maximum allowed segment sum?
answer: Feasibility is monotone: if a bound permits at most k segments, any larger bound also does. If the greedy split needs more than k, the bound is too small.

title: Split Array Largest Sum
question: How does the greedy feasibility check count segments?
answer: It extends the current segment while its sum stays within mid. When adding a value would exceed mid, it starts a new segment at that value.

title: Fizz Buzz
question: Why should divisibility by 15 be checked before divisibility by 3 or 5?
answer: A multiple of 15 is also divisible by both 3 and 5. Checking the combined case first ensures it is labeled FizzBuzz instead of only Fizz or Buzz.

title: Fizz Buzz
question: What is the time complexity of the solution?
answer: O(n) time and O(n) output space, because the loop creates one result string for each integer from 1 through n.

title: Arithmetic Slices
question: What does curr count in Arithmetic Slices?
answer: curr counts arithmetic slices ending at the current index. If the current difference continues the pattern, every prior slice extends and one new length-three slice is added.

title: Arithmetic Slices
question: Why is total incremented by curr rather than by one?
answer: When the arithmetic pattern continues, there may be multiple valid slices ending at this position, one for each qualifying suffix length. curr counts all of them.

title: Third Maximum Number
question: Why must duplicate maximum values be ignored?
answer: The task asks for the third distinct maximum. Repeated occurrences of a value do not occupy another rank.

title: Third Maximum Number
question: Why use a long sentinel in the Java implementation?
answer: Integer.MIN_VALUE is a valid input value. A sentinel outside the int range distinguishes an uninitialized third maximum from a real minimum-int value.

title: Add Strings
question: How does carry work when adding decimal strings from right to left?
answer: For each pair of digits, add both digits and the incoming carry. Append sum mod 10 and set the next carry to sum divided by 10.

title: Add Strings
question: Why are the result digits reversed before returning?
answer: Digits are appended least-significant first during right-to-left addition. Reversing the accumulated characters restores normal decimal order.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
question: Why does an odd total immediately make partitioning impossible?
answer: Two subsets with equal sums would each have to sum to total/2. If total is odd, that value is not an integer subset sum.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
question: Why does subset-sum DP iterate target sums in descending order?
answer: Descending order prevents the current number from being reused multiple times in the same iteration, which would turn the 0/1 subset problem into an unbounded one.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
question: Why does the search move to equal or higher cells when starting at an ocean border?
answer: The search reverses water flow. If water can flow from a higher cell to a lower one, the reverse search moves from the ocean inward from the lower cell to a neighbor at least as high.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
question: How are the final cells selected?
answer: A cell qualifies if it is marked reachable from both the Pacific-border search and the Atlantic-border search. The algorithm intersects those visited sets.

title: Battleships in a Board
question: Why is an X counted only when there is no X above or to the left?
answer: Every straight ship has one top-left cell. Any other X in the same ship has either an X directly above or directly to the left, so it is not counted again.

title: Battleships in a Board
question: Does the algorithm modify the board?
answer: No. It only reads each cell and its upper and left neighbors, so the original board remains unchanged.

title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
question: How does the prefix-set test decide whether a candidate XOR bit is possible?
answer: For a candidate value, each prefix p would need a partner candidate XOR p. If that partner also exists in the prefix set, two numbers can realize the candidate prefix.

title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
question: Why are bits considered from most significant to least significant?
answer: Higher bits dominate the numeric value. Greedily retaining a feasible high bit before considering lower bits maximizes the final XOR.

title: Reconstruct Original Digits from English
question: Why are digits counted in a specific dependency order?
answer: Some letters uniquely identify certain number words, such as z for zero and w for two. After those counts are known, their shared letters can be subtracted to determine the remaining digits.

title: Reconstruct Original Digits from English
question: Why is the output generated in digit order from zero through nine?
answer: The problem requires the reconstructed digits in ascending order. Repeating each digit character by its recovered count produces that canonical ordering.
